clue.text: Songs in unison for long walks of course

definitions.meaning: part-songs in which voices enter in turn, singing the same tune, like a canon
circuits played over a golf course, eighteen holes on foot

explanation.surface: Choral singing paired with long hikes, as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means a golf course: a round there is a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch sung in canon is one sense; a full circuit of the golf links is another.

clue.text: They're no go without 12

parts.note: 12 across refers to the blades used for pulling through water; these small craft cannot move without them

explanation.surface: Something that cannot function without the item from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 12 across: rowing craft go nowhere without their blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Small boats propelled by oars are useless if the oars are missing.

clue.text: Stressed that not enough goals were kicked

definitions.meaning: emphasised, marked with a line beneath

definitions.text: that not enough goals were kicked

explanation.surface: A fan complaining that the team failed to hit the net often enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into 'under' and 'scored'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise text is to put a line beneath it; scoring below par is the split reading.

clue.text: Lily of the Valley?

parts.note: Lily ... is the heroine of Trollope's The Small House at Allington; her surname is a word for a valley

explanation.surface: A question about the woodland flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower name misleads: Lily is a Trollope heroine whose surname means a valley, so she is the Lily 'of the Valley'.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern English word for a valley, and the surname of Trollope's character Lily.

clue.text: Crystal ball with sad import ?

parts.note: a clear spherical bead of liquid that signals sorrow, not a fortune-teller's globe

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's globe predicting gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crystal ball' suggests prophecy; here it is a clear drop falling from a weeping eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed in weeping is a small clear sphere that means sadness.

clue.text: Like Stoneturner's Avenue, no doubt

parts.note: plays on leaving no stone unturned and exploring every avenue: someone who turns stones has searched every avenue

explanation.surface: An address on a street named after a stonemason.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms for thoroughness are merged: one who turns over every stone has surely investigated every avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate every avenue is the idiom for a thorough search.

clue.text: Island is about to get the answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: An island is on the brink of finding the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Resolution Island lies off Baffin Island in northern Canada; another is in New Zealand's Fiordland.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution Island is a named island in the Canadian Arctic.

clue.text: To be worn with a difference, its distributor said

definitions.text: To be worn with a difference, its distributor said

parts.words: To be worn with a difference, its distributor said
parts.note: in Hamlet, Ophelia hands out herbs and says 'you must wear your ... with a difference'

explanation.surface: A garment's seller insisting it be worn in a distinctive way.
explanation.walkthrough: The distributor is Ophelia, handing out flowers and herbs in her madness in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter herb of grace that Ophelia gives away with that line.

clue.text: His turn comes after perfect play in the division

indicators.note: the shuffled piece is placed after the golf score in the answer

parts.note: par is the standard score, perfect play on a golf hole

indicators.note: a turn here means the letters of his are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's turn follows a flawless performance within his section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' shuffles HIS into ISH, and 'comes after' puts that after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrative unit of a diocese or county, a local district.

clue.text: Paradoxical pseudonym for the lexicographer

parts.note: Samuel Johnson, compiler of the great Dictionary, wrote essays under a title meaning a lazy person

explanation.surface: A puzzling pen name chosen by a dictionary-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson's essay series was named for a lazy person, a paradox for one of the most industrious writers of his age.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's periodical essays of 1758-60 bore this title, meaning a lazy loafer.

clue.text: Jemima Puddleduck made progress

parts.note: Beatrix Potter's duck moves forward the way ducks do, rocking side to side

explanation.surface: A children's-book duck getting somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Jemima Puddle-Duck is Beatrix Potter's farmyard duck; ducks walk with a rolling gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks advance on foot with a short swaying gait, so the duck moved forward that way.

clue.text: It's Louis's turn to go to grass at the institute

definitions.text: It's Louis's turn to go to grass at the institute

parts.words: It's Louis's turn to go to grass at the institute
parts.note: the French scientist Louis whose name is a rearrangement of a word for grassland gave his name to a Paris research institute

explanation.surface: Louis is due to be put out to grass at his research institute.
explanation.walkthrough: The scientist's surname rearranges a word for grazing land (that is the 'turn'), and the Paris institute is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The French chemist Louis, founder of a famous Paris research institute bearing his name.

clue.text: Resting places, when the row's over

definitions.text: Resting places, when the row's over

parts.words: Resting places, when the row's over
parts.note: row means a spell of rowing, not a quarrel; the blades are what get rested afterwards

explanation.surface: Where people go to recover after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'go' here, not 'cow': after rowing, the crew rest on their blades.
explanation.definitionFit: After rowing, the crew rest the blades: hence 'resting' them.

clue.text: Brings to mind some Franciscans about their prayers

parts.note: re means about or concerning
collects are short liturgical prayers

explanation.surface: Some friars remember things while saying their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some Franciscans' adds a second sense: the Recollects were a reformed Franciscan order. Collects are short set prayers of the church year.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall a memory is to summon it to mind again.

clue.text: Light arrangement of branches

parts.note: a branched holder for candles, giving light, not a modest display of greenery

explanation.surface: A simple flower display of twigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like 'not heavy' describing a flower arrangement; it means illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A large branched candlestick holding several candles.

clue.text: Is sorry to be without measure of anti-mosquito creams

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the words for being sorry go round the measure

parts.note: repents means feels regret, is sorry
an ell is an old cloth measure, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Someone regretting buying no insect cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, so REPENTS goes round ELL. 'without' as 'lacking' is the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotions that drive insects away are classed as repellent substances.

clue.text: Altered course with sound diplomacy

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for diplomacy is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: tact is skill and diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A diplomat changing direction with good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'sensible' describing diplomacy, but it marks the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship changes its heading by turning its bow through the wind.

clue.text: Obscure fate of Gray's rude forefathers

definitions.text: Obscure fate of Gray's rude forefathers

parts.words: Obscure fate of Gray's rude forefathers
parts.note: Gray's Elegy speaks of the rude forefathers of the hamlet and their 'homely joys

explanation.surface: The forgotten end of a poet's coarse ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard has the phrase 'destiny obscure' for the villagers' lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate and lot are synonyms for what life has in store; Gray's line pairs it with obscure.

clue.text: Framley-ish ?

parts.note: Trollope's novel Framley Parsonage; an adjective in the manner of that house means clerical

explanation.surface: Something in the manner of a village called Framley.
explanation.walkthrough: Framley Parsonage is a Trollope novel; the adjective formed from a parsonage means like a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a clergyman, as a parsonage or vicarage does.

clue.text: Underlines the importance of pressure groups

definitions.meaning: read literally as several kinds of pressure, strains and tensions

explanation.surface: A lobby makes its priorities clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressure groups' looks like lobbies; it means pressures in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise is one sense; strains or tensions in plural is the other.

clue.text: Team magazine

definitions.meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: A sports club's own publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a north London football club; 'magazine' is a weapons store, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A London football club, and an armoury or arms depot.

clue.text: Quite candid this sprig of the nobility is to the French

parts.note: Hon., short for Honourable, is the courtesy title of a peer's child
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A young aristocrat speaks frankly in French company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the children of peers are styled 'the Honourable', abbreviated Hon.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank and truthful is a synonym for candour.

clue.text: He may receive another cheeky offer

definitions.text: He may receive another cheeky offer

parts.words: He may receive another cheeky offer
parts.note: from the Gospel: whoever hits you on one cheek, turn the other to him

explanation.surface: Someone getting a second impudent proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheeky' means involving a cheek: the one who strikes is offered the other cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: One who strikes a blow, as in 'turn the other cheek' to the one who hits you.

clue.text: Relish a kiss ?

definitions.meaning: a taste or flavour, as in 'a hint of'
a loud kiss on the lips

explanation.surface: Enjoying a peck on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb meaning enjoy; it is a noun for a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight flavour or trace is one sense; a loud kiss is the other.

clue.text: Miss Matty ? Not at Cranford!

parts.note: Gaskell's gentle Miss Matty is no busybody, though the gossipy ladies of Cranford around her are

explanation.surface: A question about a character from Mrs Gaskell's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cranford is Elizabeth Gaskell's novel of genteel village ladies; the clue asks whether 'Miss Matty' (read as mischievous meddling) suits her, and answers no.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying and interfering, as the gossips of Cranford are thought to be.

clue.text: Hollow warning

definitions.meaning: a hole in a hillside or rock
Latin for beware, the British schoolboy call that a master is coming

explanation.surface: An empty threat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public-school slang 'cave!' (Latin, beware) was shouted to warn that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavern in rock is one sense; the Latin school cry 'beware' is the other.

clue.text: Bravo William, you've a part to acknowledge

indicators.note: the letters needed are a part of the words bravo William, run across the gap

explanation.surface: Praising William for owning up to his role.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or admit openly is to confess and own up.

clue.text: No art in ruined Palace

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A palace in ruins has lost its works of art.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand and Petit Trianon are palaces in the grounds of Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trianon is a royal residence in the park at Versailles.

clue.text: Americans in cahoots for a start

indicators.note: only the start of the word cahoots is wanted, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Americans conspiring from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Inc. (incorporated) follows a US company name, as Ltd does in Britain: firms of partners in cahoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The US abbreviation for an incorporated company, where business partners join forces.

clue.text: Alph ran through them

parts.note: Coleridge's Kubla Khan: 'Where Alph, the sacred river

explanation.surface: A runner called Alph passing through some places.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph is the sacred river of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's river flows through huge underground hollows.

clue.text: Here's a wrinkle on the bag for a hiker

definitions.text: Here's a wrinkle on the bag for a hiker

indicators.note: the wrinkle word sits on top of, before, the bag word

parts.note: a ruck is a crease or wrinkle in cloth
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A tip about which bag a walker should carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkle' also means a handy tip, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker's backpack, carried on the shoulders.

clue.text: Inundates the marshes

explanation.surface: Floods the wetlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood or overwhelm is one sense; bogs and fens are the other.
